column1: # The artifacts a scheduled run can re-fetch unattended, and how.
# NOT every pinned artifact. Most of the corpus is reachable only
# through a human step — a repository checked out at a pinned commit, a
# distribution package unpacked, an archive whose member is the thing
# that is pinned — and inventing a URL for those would produce a monitor
# that reported failures about its own guesses. A row here is a promise
# that one HTTP GET returns the pinned bytes after the stated
# normalization, and nothing else.
# The complement is the interesting half and the monitor reports it: an
# artifact with no row has no unattended refresh route, which is a fact
# about this corpus worth knowing rather than a gap to hide.
# normalize:
#   none      the response body IS the artifact
#   strip-cr  the response body with carriage returns removed. One
#             vendor serves its certificate chains CRLF and the others
#             LF; a Nim triple-quoted literal in an LF file cannot carry
#             the carriage returns, so the pin is of the stripped form.
#             Applying it to all three chains is deliberate — it is a
#             no-op on the two that are already LF, and a rule with an
#             exception is a rule somebody gets wrong.
# name
KdsMilanChainPem
KdsMilanCrlDerHex
KdsGenoaChainPem
KdsGenoaCrlDerHex
KdsTurinChainPem
KdsTurinCrlDerHex
IntelSgxRootCaDerHex
